# Filemark — project rules

Portable instructions that extend the global rules. Keep short; prune when a rule stops firing on real work.

## Repo topology (CLAUDE.md + docsi via repolink)

- **This `CLAUDE.md` and `docsi/` both live in the private-repo** at `/Volumes/D/www/projects/khanakia/private-repo/markdown-viewer-chrome-ext/`. They are **symlinked into `filemark/`** via the [`repolink`](https://github.com/thesatellite-ai/repolink-go) CLI — so the source of truth is the private-repo, and filemark imports both.
- `docsi/` holds planning / problem docs: `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `PROBLEM.md`, `TASKS.md`, `TECH.md`, `PUBLISHING.md`, `README-GUIDELINES.md`. Name is literally `docsi` (short for "docs internal"), *not* `docs` — it's a private space, not public project docs.
- Both `CLAUDE.md` and `docsi/` are in `filemark/.gitignore` (repolink-managed block) and never enter filemark's git history. Public docs for filemark live in filemark's own `README.md` + (future) `/docs` in the repo.
- **Edit from either path** — both resolve to the same inode. In filemark, `cat docsi/PROBLEM.md` and `cat /Volumes/D/.../private-repo/markdown-viewer-chrome-ext/docsi/PROBLEM.md` are the same file.
- **Adding more shared files from private-repo → filemark:** `cd filemark && repolink link markdown-viewer-chrome-ext/<src> <dst>` (source path is relative to private-repo root). The auto-gitignore block keeps them out of commits.
- **Breaking a symlink**: `repolink unlink <name> --yes && repolink cleanup --yes` from inside filemark. Sources in private-repo are never touched — repolink only manipulates the link files.
- **Fresh clone of filemark on a new machine:** requires installing `repolink` + `repolink setup` on the private-repo, then `repolink` (bare) inside filemark restores the symlinks. Without this, both `CLAUDE.md` and `docsi/` will be missing.
- Memory for Claude about this layout lives in `~/.claude/projects/-Volumes-D-www-projects-khanakia-private-repo-markdown-viewer-chrome-ext/memory/code_location.md`.

## Authoring brainstorm / planning docs (`docsi/`)

- **Always invoke the `/filemark` skill** before writing or editing any brainstorm, plan, problem, roadmap, ADR, or component-spec doc inside `docsi/` (private-repo). These files are read in filemark, so they must use the correct component grammar (`<Callout>`, `<Tabs>`, `<Details>`, `<Stats>`, `<ADR>`, `<Datagrid>`, `<Chart>`, `<Kanban>`, `<TaskList>`, `<TaskStats>`, `<TaskTimeline>`, sigil task bullets, filter DSL) and observe the two HTML-in-markdown survival rules.
- Applies to **every file under `docsi/`** — `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `PROBLEM.md`, `TASKS.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `*_PLAN.md`, `*_ADR.md`, future docs.
- **Does NOT apply to public docs inside the filemark repo itself** — `filemark/README.md`, future `filemark/docs/**`, package READMEs, and any `*.md` checked into the public git history. Those are GitHub-rendered and must stay portable plain-markdown (no filemark-specific components).
- If `/filemark` skill not loaded in the session, load it first before drafting; do not freehand filemark components from memory.

## Styling

- **Tailwind utilities first.** Every shell component in `apps/chrome-ext/` and every viewer package should default to Tailwind classes on JSX. Raw CSS classes (`.fv-*`) are reserved for *rendered content* where an external library (react-markdown, react-json-view) owns the DOM and Tailwind utilities can't be injected inline. MDX body typography is the only accepted `fv-*` in `apps/chrome-ext/src/styles/index.css`.
- **Package-local styles stay in the package.** If a viewer package (`packages/json-viewer`, `packages/mdx-viewer`, future) needs styles, use Tailwind utilities on its JSX or a co-located `.css` the package imports. Do **not** hoist per-package CSS into `apps/chrome-ext/src/styles/index.css`. The host stylesheet only carries app-wide tokens + MDX body typography.
- **shadcn tokens are the palette.** Always style with `bg-muted`, `text-foreground`, `border`, `text-destructive`, etc. Never write `bg-gray-900` or `#0f1115` inline — those break theme switching.
- **Dark mode via `@custom-variant dark (&:is([data-theme="dark"], …))`.** shadcn's `.dark` selector maps to our `[data-theme="dark"]` attribute. Don't add a `.dark` class manually anywhere.

## Viewer packages (portability)

- **No `chrome.*`, `vscode.*`, or Node built-ins inside `packages/**`.** Host-specific concerns arrive via `ViewerProps` (`storage`, `assets`, `onNavigate`). A future VS Code host should drop in the same package unchanged.
- **Host theme via `useThemeOptional()`**, not `useTheme()`. Packages must not crash when rendered outside a `ThemeProvider`.
- **Externalize peer + optional deps in `tsup.config.ts`.** Everything that pnpm's workspace provides (`react`, `react-dom`, `@filemark/core`, and any library packaged with the host) should be listed in `external`. Don't re-bundle `@uiw/react-json-view`, `shiki`, `yaml`, etc.
- **MV3 CSP rules out `unsafe-eval`.** Do not pull in libraries that rely on `new Function()` / `eval` (ruled out `@mdx-js/mdx` `evaluate` and `gray-matter` for this reason). If you absolutely need eval, it lives in a sandboxed iframe — not the extension page.

## Base UI / basecn quirks

- **Tooltip, Popover, DropdownMenu `…Content` must wrap Portal + Positioner internally.** The registry ships bare `Popup`s; using them without Positioner throws `Base UI error #71`. Every basecn Content wrapper in this repo is patched to include Portal + Positioner — preserve that when re-adding or re-generating a component.
- **Prefer `children` over `render={<Component/>}` for triggers.** Passing a nested provider tree (e.g. `<Tooltip>` inside a `PopoverTrigger render={...}`) confuses `useRender` and throws `#31`. Keep triggers as direct elements or plain buttons with `title=` attributes.
- **Menu primitives are fussy.** For simple action lists, use Popover + plain `<button>` rows instead of DropdownMenu. `FileActions` does this.

## Chrome extension

- **MV3 CSP rules out `unsafe-eval`.** See above.
- **Content script is a classic script, no imports.** Entry `content.js` is pinned by filename in `vite.config.ts` and referenced by name in `manifest.json` — if you rename one, rename the other.
- **`sessionStorage["fv-handled"]` guards re-entry** in the content script, preventing the redirect bounce-back loop. Don't remove.
- **FSA API hides absolute paths.** Folder-picked files must either have a user-pasted `rootPath` (FSA path) or `sourceUrl` from `file://` interception for "Open in editor" / "Reveal in Finder" to work. Chrome security — there is no workaround.
- **`dataTransfer.files` + `items[].webkitGetAsEntry()` are complementary, not interchangeable.** Directories show up only via `items/webkitGetAsEntry`; files show up in both but `webkitGetAsEntry` returns null in synthetic DataTransfer. Read files from `.files`, use entries only for directory detection.

## Library / store

- **Recent list is stable.** A file keeps its slot once added; clicking an existing recent does *not* move it to the top. Users rely on muscle memory.
- **Drop folders mark `kind: "drop"`.** The "Reconnect folder" button is reserved for `kind: "fsa"` since drop-folders have no handle to reconnect.
- **`remark-breaks` is on.** Single newlines in prose become hard breaks so ASCII trees and tables-in-paragraphs render faithfully. Authors can still double-newline for paragraph breaks.

## Task-first workflow

- **Every actionable request from the user becomes a task before any code changes.** Bug, feature, refactor, polish, doc edit, infra change, dependency bump — anything that produces a diff or a deploy. Capture it first in `docsi/TASKS.md` (or the relevant `docsi/*_PLAN.md` if one exists for that feature area) under the appropriate milestone or backlog section, with full filemark sigils: `(milestone-or-project)`, `!priority`, `^task-…` ID, `after:` deps if known.
- **Order of operations:** (1) write the task line in the right `docsi/*.md` file, (2) only then implement, (3) flip to `[/]` while in progress, (4) `[x]` =YYYY-MM-DD on completion. The TASKS file is the running log of what was done and why.
- If the request is exploratory ("what could we…?", "should we…?") it stays a discussion until the user gives an imperative. Only then capture-as-task and implement.
- Tiny one-line edits the user clearly wants done in the same breath (`fix typo`, `bump version`) can skip the task-first step. Use judgement — if it's worth a commit, it's probably worth a task.
- Mirror also into the in-conversation `TaskCreate` tool when the work needs multi-step tracking (e.g. multiple files, multiple builds), so progress is visible inside the session too.

## Commit etiquette

- Follow the global rule: ask before committing, never auto-push, never mention Claude/AI/Anthropic in messages.
- Keep commit messages structured: short subject (≤70 chars), then a body with bullet groups by subsystem.

## When in doubt

Favor small, reversible changes. Build after every structural edit (`pnpm --filter chrome-ext build`), verify in the extension (`chrome://extensions` → reload on the Filemark card), and only commit when a feature is demonstrably working.
